## Reproduced on macOS (Sequoia) — fresh clone to different path

Hit this today. I had a previous clone of opencode at one path, deleted it, and re-cloned to a different path. Desktop matched the new project to the old DB record correctly (via git remote fingerprint), but all existing sessions still carry the old absolute path in the session table. Every prompt immediately fails with:

```
PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (<old-path>)
(cause: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '<old-path>')

```
The project_directory table is updated correctly to the new path — the bug is that session.path and session.directory are never migrated when the project record's directory changes. The fix would be to cascade the path update from project_directory down to all sessions sharing the same project_id at the point the new directory is accepted.

Confirmed the orphaned sessions are recoverable via direct SQL:
```
UPDATE session
SET path = '<new-relative-path>',
    directory = '<new-absolute-path>'
WHERE directory = '<old-absolute-path>';
```
This solves an actual issue. Thank you for fixing this!
Any solution for this? Or workaround

I can corroborate this at the provider-transport boundary on OpenCode 1.18.3 and 1.18.4.

Using an isolated `opencode serve` plus a loopback OpenAI-compatible SSE provider, I start an actual configured-model turn, wait until the provider emits a valid partial chat-completion SSE frame, then call `POST /api/session/:id/interrupt`.

Observed on both versions:

- interrupt returns 204
- `/api/session/active` removes the session
- the loopback provider request receives neither request `aborted` nor response `close` within 5 seconds
- this reproduces for both a queued and a steered delivery (2 provider requests total)
- no external provider is contacted

So the application state is cleaned up, but the in-flight provider HTTP/SSE stream remains alive. That leaves a path for a late provider tool call like the one in this issue to arrive after cancellation.

The relevant cancellation files are unchanged from v1.18.3 through v1.18.4 and current `dev` at `4cc022481c184cb9d5e14f7e882b6749d2414553`:

- `packages/core/src/session/run-coordinator.ts`
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`
- `packages/llm/src/route/transport/http.ts`

Expected invariant: once interrupt completes, the provider response body/socket is cancelled promptly and no later provider event can be admitted or execute a tool. I can provide the self-contained TypeScript probe and secret-free JSON reports if useful.
Any solutions for this yet?

Following up on this with hard evidence from testing on opencode v1.18.3 (Windows x64 binary).

What works
The TUI slot system exists internally — confirmed by extracting strings from opencode.exe:
- Slot names: sidebar_content, sidebar_title, sidebar_footer, home_footer, home_bottom, home_prompt, session_prompt, session_prompt_right, app, app_bottom, home_logo
- Built-in feature plugin IDs: internal:sidebar-mcp, internal:sidebar-lsp, internal:sidebar-todo, internal:sidebar-context, internal:sidebar-files, internal:sidebar-footer, internal:home-footer, internal:home-tips
- The TuiPluginRuntime module is compiled in, exporting init/dispose/list/installPlugin/addPlugin/activatePlugin/deactivatePlugin/createLegacyTuiPluginHost

What doesn't work
Local plugins in ~/.config/opencode/plugins/*.ts(x) can export a tui function and it gets invoked — but the api argument only contains server-side fields:

api keys: $, client, directory, experimental_workspace, project, serverUrl, worktree

api.slots is undefined. api.ui, api.desktop, api.unsafe — all undefined.

Tried env flags OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL, OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_EVENT_SYSTEM, OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORKSPACES — none of them unlock slot access for external plugins.

Ask
Is enabling TUI slot injection for external plugins on the roadmap? The internal feature-plugins/sidebar/*.tsx pattern (api.slots.register({ order, slots: { sidebar_content() { ... } } })) is exactly what we'd need. Even a single experimental flag to expose api.slots to local plugins would unlock this entire class of use cases (custom status indicators, skill usage tracking, session metrics, etc.) without changing the architecture.

Happy to help test any experimental build that exposes this.

thanks for the review, merged the refactor PR (FahadBinHussain#2) into this branch — createTimeoutController is now live, both call sites in tools.ts are down to 3 lines each. cleaned up a stray duplicate jsdoc block + unused import that came along with the merge, 15/15 tests still passing.

on the two other points:

- **type safety**: checked this — config values go through Schema.optional(PositiveInt) at decode time (packages/core/src/v1/config/config.ts + agent.ts), so a string like "60000" fails schema validation before esolve() ever sees it. the ?? fallback in resolve() only ever receives a valid number or undefined, not a raw unvalidated value. no guard needed there.
- **naming**: checked the codebase for 	ool_timeout_ms / 	ool_timeout_sec — neither exists anywhere in anomalyco/opencode (confirmed via GitHub code search + local grep on a fresh clone of dev). so there's no actual naming collision with xperimental.tool_timeout / xperimental.task_timeout. happy to rename if a maintainer prefers it, but it's not fixing a real conflict.
